title: DELETE can silently erase an active processing job

evidence.quote: if digest: session.delete(digest); session.commit() ... return {"status": "deleted", "filename": filename, "note": "File already removed"}
digest = session.get(Digest, self.digest_id); if digest: digest.status = "completed" ... session.commit()

reasoning: Digest generation creates a processing Digest row with the final filename before the EPUB exists. delete_digest has no status check, deletes that row, and returns success when the file is missing. The worker's later progress and completion updates are guarded by if digest, so after the row is deleted they become no-ops while the background job can still generate files and articles with no parent digest record.
reproduction: Start a digest, obtain its processing filename from the digest list, then call DELETE /api/digests/{filename} before generation completes. The route removes the processing row and reports deleted even though the worker is still running.
recommendation: Only allow filename-based deletion for completed or failed digests, or implement an explicit cancellation flow that coordinates with the worker. For processing rows, return 409 Conflict unless cancellation is actually supported.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exercise DELETE against processing digests or worker interaction; existing tests do not cover delete_digest at all.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that inserts a Digest with status='processing' and no output file, calls DELETE /api/digests/{filename}, asserts 409, and asserts the Digest row remains.
minimumFixScope: Add a status guard in delete_digest and cover processing-state behavior with an API test.
